papers.title: Momentum Contrast-Enhanced Multimodal Representation Learning for Drug Synergy Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate prediction of synergistic drug combinations can accelerate anticancer combination discovery. Existing methods inadequately model higher-order drug–drug–cell-line interactions and drug–disease associations and remain sensitive to sparse and noisy multi-omics data, limiting generalization to unseen cell lines and drug combinations. Results We present MoCo-MultiSynergy, a multimodal framework that combines modality-specific momentum contrastive learning with heterogeneous hypergraph modeling. The hypergraph represents synergistic drug–drug–cell-line triplets and drug–disease associations, while gated residual propagation refines node representations. Momentum Contrast modules regularize encoded drug and cell-line representations using latent feature masking and Gaussian perturbation. On the O’Neil and NCI-ALMANAC datasets, MoCo-MultiSynergy achieves the highest AUROC and AUPRC across the evaluated settings, with the largest gains when generalizing to unseen cell lines and drug combinations. Availability and implementation Source code is available at https://github.com/27167199/MoCo-MultiSynergy

Existing methods inadequately model higher-order drug-drug-cell-line interactions and drug-disease associations and remain sensitive to sparse and noisy multi-omics data, limiting generalization to unseen cell lines and drug combinations.

RESULTS: We present MoCo-MultiSynergy, a multimodal framework that combines modality-specific momentum contrastive learning with heterogeneous hypergraph modeling. The hypergraph represents synergistic drug-drug-cell-line triplets and drug-disease associations, while gated residual propagation refines node representations. Momentum Contrast modules regularize encoded drug and cell-line representations using latent feature masking and Gaussian perturbation. On the O'Neil and NCI-ALMANAC datasets, MoCo-MultiSynergy achieves the highest AUROC and AUPRC across the evaluated settings, with the largest gains when generalizing to unseen cell lines and drug combinations.

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 准确预测协同药物组合可以加速抗癌组合的发现。
llm_highlights_zh: 现有方法不足以模拟高阶药物-药物-细胞系相互作用和药物-疾病关联，并且对稀疏和嘈杂的多组学数据仍然敏感，限制了对看不见的细胞系和药物组合的泛化。
我们提出了 MoCo-MultiSynergy，这是一种多模态框架，它将模态特定动量对比学习与异构超图建模相结合。
超图表示协同药物-药物-细胞系三联体和药物-疾病关联，而门控残差传播则细化节点表示。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 准确预测协同药物组合可以加速抗癌组合的发现。现有方法不足以模拟高阶药物-药物-细胞系相互作用和药物-疾病关联，并且对稀疏和嘈杂的多组学数据仍然敏感，限制了对看不见的细胞系和药物组合的泛化。结果我们提出了 MoCo-MultiSynergy，这是一个多模态框架，它将特定模态动量对比学习与异构超图建模相结合。超图代表协同药物-药物-细胞系三元组和药物-疾病关联，而门控残差传播则细化了节点表示。动量对比模块使用潜在特征掩蔽和高斯扰动对编码药物和细胞系表示进行正则化。在 O’Neil 和 NCI-ALMANAC 数据集上，MoCo-MultiSynergy 在评估的设置中实现了最高的 AUROC 和 AUPRC，在推广到未见过的细胞系和药物组合时收益最大。可用性和实施​​ 源代码可在 https://github.com/27167199/MoCo-MultiSynergy 获取

papers.title: Spatio-DARLIN maps cell state and clonal history in intact mouse tissues
papers.summary: Spatio-DARLIN combines high-diversity genetic lineage tracing with spatial transcriptomics to record cell lineage, gene expression and location in the same tissue section. This approach reliably recovers thousands of clones in mouse intestine and brain, revealing how clonal architecture delineates tissue development and homeostasis

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Accurate prediction of synergistic drug combinations can accelerate anticancer combination discovery. Existing methods inadequately model higher-order drug–drug–cell-line interactions and drug–disease associations and remain sensitive to sparse and noisy multi-omics data, limiting generalization to unseen cell lines and drug combinations. Results We present MoCo-MultiSynergy, a multimodal framework that combines modality-specific momentum contrastive learning with heterogeneous hypergraph modeling. The hypergraph represents synergistic drug–drug–cell-line triplets and drug–disease associations, while gated residual propagation refines node representations. Momentum Contrast modules regularize encoded drug and cell-line representations using latent feature masking and Gaussian perturbation. On the O’Neil and NCI-ALMANAC datasets, MoCo-MultiSynergy achieves the highest AUROC and AUPRC across the evaluated settings, with the largest gains when generalizing to unseen cell lines and drug combinations.
